title: 茶水间英文 - 10月6日 | 马斯克重回万亿、欧洲AI叫板中国、外星球来电了
hook: Musk's back in the trillion club, Europe crashes the AI race, and scientists hear a distant world hum.
summary: 马斯克身家重回一万亿美元；欧洲 Mistral 叫板中美 AI 竞赛；科学家首次“听到”系外行星的极光电波。
vocab: 情绪大起大落；反复无常

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Hey everyone, welcome back to the show. It is Tuesday, October sixth, and I am Alex.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And I am Jordan. We have got three fresh stories for you today, plus our silly little question at the end. Let us get into it.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: First up, the money story everyone is talking about. Elon Musk is a trillionaire again.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Again? How many times has this man joined the trillionaire club?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: His fortune jumped by sixty-five billion dollars to one point zero four trillion dollars, thanks to Tesla stock climbing almost seven percent and SpaceX shares jumping thirteen percent since the start of October.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: One point zero four trillion. I cannot even picture that number. That is like, what, a million million?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: A thousand billions, if that helps. And he is not the only winner. The Nasdaq stock index closed at a record high yesterday, and the S and P five hundred is less than one percent away from its own record.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So the market is basically partying. Oil prices fell a bit, bond yields pulled back from a twenty-four year high, and suddenly everyone feels rich again.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Exactly. It is the classic Wall Street mood swing. One week everyone is nervous, the next week it is champagne.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Well, not everyone. My wallet did not get the memo.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Ha. Fair enough. But here is your line for the watercooler. Did you hear Elon Musk is a trillionaire again? One point zero four trillion dollars. Wild.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Okay, story number two, and this one is about the global A I race heating up.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Oh, I like this one. Europe just crashed the party.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: That is right. Arthur Mensch, the C E O of the French A I company Mistral, said on Tuesday that their brand new model beats Chinese models on cybersecurity, and the full reveal is coming later today.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Mistral is only three years old, but people call it Europe's top contender in the A I race. They raised three billion euros last month at a twenty-one billion euro valuation.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And Mensch had a real mic drop moment. He said the narrative that Europe cannot compete is simply not true.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The timing is perfect, because a new analysis just found that China has almost caught up with America. Chinese models now trail the top American ones by only three percent on key tests, down from fifteen percent earlier this year.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: That is thanks to DeepSeek's latest model, which scored eighty-one point one on a major benchmark. Still, only three of the top fifteen models worldwide are Chinese, and rankings change fast.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: So now it is a three-way race. America, China, and Europe all swinging. Your stealable line. So apparently Europe's top A I lab says its new model beats the Chinese ones on cyber. The A I race just got a third runner.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: And for our lighter closer today, we are going to space. Kind of.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Oh no, are we doing aliens again? Listeners, I promise, Alex brings up aliens every month.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Not aliens this time. Well, probably not aliens. Astronomers have detected the first ever radio signal coming directly from a planet outside our solar system.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Wait, for real? Like, a planet beaming us a message?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: A gas giant called Beta Pictoris b, about sixty-three light-years away and twelve times the mass of Jupiter. But before you get excited, the scientists say it is not little green men. It is auroras.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Auroras? Like the northern lights?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Exactly like that, except this planet's magnetic field is at least two hundred times stronger than Jupiter's. So its light show is off the charts. A Harvard astronomer named Edo Berger said he knows radio signals make people think of aliens, but this is something very different.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Sixty-three light-years away and we can hear its magnetic field humming. That is honestly kind of beautiful.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: It is the first time we have ever measured a magnetic field on another world. Your line for today. Have you heard? Scientists picked up a radio signal from a planet sixty-three light-years away. Not aliens, sadly. Just the universe's biggest light show.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Time for today's random question. If your life had a theme song that played every time you walked into a room, what would yours be?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Easy. The Imperial March. The Darth Vader music. I enter the office kitchen, the music swells, everyone freezes.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Deeply dramatic for a man making instant noodles.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The noodles deserve drama. Yours?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: A kazoo attempting something heroic. Epic in my head, ridiculous out loud.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: So I am a movie villain and you are a party favor with big dreams? Steal this one today and ask a friend. The answers tell you everything.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That is all for today, folks. Thanks for hanging out with us.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: We will be back tomorrow with more stories to steal for your small talk. See you then.

title: 茶水间英文 - 10月7日 | 梅西谢幕战、芯片豪赌、Uber大收购
hook: Messi bids farewell, SpaceX bets $40B on chips, and Uber buys your lunch.
summary: 梅西踢完阿根廷国家队谢幕战；SpaceX 拟筹 400 亿美元押注 AI 芯片；Uber 23 亿美元收购企业订餐公司 EzCater。

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome to Tea Break English. It is Wednesday, October seventh, and this is the show that gets you ready for small talk in about five minutes. I am Alex.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And I am Jordan. Three big stories today, one ready-to-steal line for each, and then a ridiculous question to end on. Let us get into it.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Story number one, and honestly, the story of the week. Lionel Messi played his very last game for Argentina last night.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Twenty-one years, two hundred and eight games, one hundred and twenty-six goals. And the final act was perfect. A friendly against Benin in Buenos Aires, Argentina won three to zero, and Messi scored one and set up the other two.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: One goal, two assists, in front of eighty-five thousand people at the Monumental stadium. He wiped away tears as he walked off, and then a drone show lit up the sky above the stadium to say goodbye.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Argentines have been dreading this for years. People there say, thank God they were born in the era of Messi.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: And here is your stealable line. Did you hear Messi played his last game for Argentina? One goal, two assists, and a drone show send-off. Not a bad way to say goodbye.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Story number two. Forty billion dollars. That is what SpaceX is trying to raise, according to the Financial Times.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The plan is ten billion in bank loans plus thirty billion in investment-grade debt, led by the asset manager Apollo, and the money goes straight to Nvidia for A I chips.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: The rocket company is becoming an A I company. Musk says the Colossus data centers will use Nvidia hardware exclusively, and the new Colossus two could more than double its chip count by December.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The scale of the spending is wild. Morgan Stanley estimates that A I infrastructure will need one point five trillion dollars in outside financing by twenty twenty-eight.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So basically, everyone is mortgaging the future to buy chips. Steal this line. So apparently SpaceX is raising forty billion dollars just to buy Nvidia chips. The A I gold rush is eating everyone's lunch.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Story number three, and this one is personal for anyone who orders lunch at work. Uber is buying ezCater, the office catering platform, for two point three billion dollars in cash.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: EzCater lets companies order food from over one hundred and forty thousand restaurants for meetings and office events. The average order is over four hundred dollars. Your lunch order is pocket change next to that.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The company handled over two point five billion dollars in bookings last year. Uber wants to plug it into Uber Eats and Uber for Business, and honestly this is about catching up with DoorDash, which still owns the American delivery market.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And Uber is not done shopping. It is still working on that fourteen point eight billion dollar bid for Delivery Hero. Nobody in this economy is going hungry.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Stealable line. Did you see Uber just bought a catering company for two point three billion? Your next team lunch might come from Uber Eats.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: All right, time for the random question. Alex, if you could instantly become world-class at one completely useless skill, what would it be?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Whistling. Not cute whistling. Concert-level, four-octave, make-the-dogs-cry whistling. Every room I enter, whistling. I would be the instant celebrity of every grocery store line.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Mine would be solving a Rubik's cube with my feet. No practical use, nobody asked for it, but imagine the party trick at a dinner table.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Whose dinner table has room for foot cube solving?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Every dinner table, once they see me. That is the whole point.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Okay listeners, steal this one today. Ask a friend what useless skill they would master. You will learn something weird, I promise.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: That is your five minutes. Three stories, three stealable lines, one useless skill.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: See you tomorrow morning for more watercooler ammunition. Bye!

title: 茶水间英文 - 10月8日 | 好莱坞大合并、大空头唱衰AI、道奇约战酿酒人
hook: Hollywood's $110B merger, the Big Short guy vs. AI, and Dodgers vs. Brewers.
summary: 派拉蒙 1100 亿美元完成对华纳兄弟的收购；《大空头》原型 Michael Burry 唱衰 AI 泡沫；道奇与酿酒人会师国联冠军赛。
vocab: 不用动脑的选择；显而易见
大卫战歌利亚；以小搏大

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome back to Watercooler Chat. I am Alex.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And I am Jordan. It is Thursday, October eighth, and we have three juicy stories to get you chat-ready.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: We sure do. Paramount has officially completed its takeover of Warner Brothers, and the price tag is one hundred ten billion dollars.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: One hundred ten billion. That is the no-brainer headline of the week. And here is the twist. They are not calling it Paramount anymore. The whole combined company is now called Skydance.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Right. David Ellison, the producer behind Top Gun Maverick, is now the chairman and C E O, and he controls Paramount Pictures, Warner Brothers, H B O, C N N, C B S, Paramount Plus, and H B O Max.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And the toy box is unreal. Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, D C Comics, Star Trek, SpongeBob. One company now owns most of your childhood.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The scale is wild. Nearly seventy billion in yearly revenue, more than two hundred million subscribers, and six billion in cost savings targeted over three years.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: They promise it will make the company leaner and more nimble, which is corporate speak for fewer desks.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: True. But we might finally get one streaming app instead of two, and I would love to pay only once. Here is your line to steal today. Did you hear Paramount just bought Warner Brothers for one hundred ten billion dollars? One company now owns Harry Potter, Batman, and SpongeBob.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Story number two is a total mood swing from yesterday. The guy from The Big Short has entered the chat.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Michael Burry. The investor who called the housing crash in two thousand eight. He just wrote on Substack that all of this A I spending could end up as sunk cost.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Sunk cost. Money you spend and never get back. His argument is something he calls compression. Once A I gets cheaper to run, he thinks all these giant data centers will not be worth what they cost.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: He also says Open A I and Anthropic are trying to muscle into Big Tech's oligopoly, but he doubts it is sustainable, and he sees a sizable market correction coming in the next few months.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Meanwhile, Nvidia keeps hitting record highs. The market is going full speed ahead, and Burry is standing on the tracks waving a red flag.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Perfect watercooler material. You sound smart no matter which side you take. Here is your line to steal. So apparently the Big Short guy thinks all this A I spending could become sunk cost. Is the A I boom a gold rush or a bubble?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And for our third story, let us head to the ballpark, because October baseball just got very spicy.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Spicy is the word. The National League Championship Series is set, and it is a rematch. The Milwaukee Brewers against the Los Angeles Dodgers.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: The Brewers beat the Padres three games to one last night in San Diego. And the Dodgers beat the Braves four to one in Atlanta.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: This is classic David versus Goliath. Small market versus big market. The Dodgers are chasing their third straight World Series title, while the Brewers have never won a championship. Not once.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Over in the American League, the Rays just swept the Yankees. Three games, zero wins for New York. Yankees fans are melting down as we speak.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: And the White Sox lead the Guardians two games to one, after Cleveland punched back with a nine to three win last night. Game four is tonight in Chicago.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So much baseball. Here is your line to steal. Have you seen the playoff picture? The Brewers and Dodgers are facing off again, and the Rays just swept the Yankees. October baseball never disappoints.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Time for our random question of the day. If you could mute one everyday sound forever, what would it be?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Oh, easy. The alarm clock. That sound is pure evil.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Fair, but mine is the microwave beep. It keeps beeping like it has a personal grudge against me.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Ha. What about the leaf blower? My neighbor fires his up at eight A M on Saturdays.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Okay, that wins. Actually, no. The seatbelt ding in the car. It judges you for a full thirty seconds.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: True. Listeners, your turn. What sound would you mute forever? Ask a friend today.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That is it for today, friends. Tomorrow we are back with fresh stories and a brand new random question to keep your small talk sharp.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: See you in the morning.

title: 茶水间英文 - 10月9日 | 和平奖揭晓、OpenAI营收乌龙、咖啡配卷饼
hook: Nobel Prize drama, OpenAI's $20B oopsie, and coffee meets burrito.
summary: 诺贝尔和平奖揭晓；OpenAI 营收预期上演 200 亿美元乌龙反转；星巴克前 CEO 或推动与 Chipotle 合并，咖啡配卷饼？
vocab: 起立鼓掌；经久不息的掌声
大起大落；像过山车一样
同类比较；在同一基准上
用钱包投票；用消费表态

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and happy Friday. It is Friday, October ninth. I am Alex.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And I am Jordan. It is the weekend eve, so our brains are already halfway to the couch. But first, three stories to make you sound smart at dinner tonight, plus our random question at the end.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: The Nobel Peace Prize. It was just announced, and it went to an eighty-five-year-old human rights lawyer from South Africa named Navi Pillay.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Eighty-five and winning a Nobel Prize. I can barely get out of bed without groaning.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And her life story is incredible. She was born in South Africa during apartheid, became one of the first women to open her own law practice there, and defended activists fighting apartheid, including people connected to Nelson Mandela.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: And here is the funny part. When the news broke, she was at a conference in Germany, and the room gave her a long standing ovation.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And she joked, if you clap a little bit more, maybe I will share the prize with you. Here is your small talk line for story one. Did you hear who won the Nobel Peace Prize? An eighty-five-year-old lawyer who spent her life fighting apartheid. Proof that it is never too late to get your flowers. Story two. The artificial intelligence market had a week like a roller coaster, and it all came down to one confusing number.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: I saw this. On Thursday, a report said OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, told investors its annualized revenue was about fifty billion dollars, not the seventy billion people were expecting.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Twenty billion dollars lower. Markets panicked. Chip stocks like Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Oracle all fell hard. People started asking, is the AI bubble finally popping?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Then the plot twist. On Friday, a different report said OpenAI actually expects to reach seventy billion dollars or more in annualized revenue by year end. So markets flipped right back up. Turns out the whole scare was basically an accounting question.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Explain that in plain English.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: OpenAI counts its revenue differently from its rival Anthropic. Anthropic includes money that comes through cloud partners like Amazon and Google. OpenAI does not. So the two numbers were never apples to apples. A twenty-billion-dollar gap, one scary headline, one reassuring headline, and billions of dollars of market value moved on a footnote. Here is your stealable line. Did you see what happened with OpenAI's revenue numbers? One report sent chip stocks tumbling, the next day another report sent them right back up. It was just an accounting difference. Story three, and this one is fun. Starbucks has been exploring a takeover of Chipotle.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: My morning coffee and my lunch burrito, from the same company? My wallet just got nervous.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Starbucks has been working with advisers on a takeover proposal for Chipotle, which is worth almost thirty-nine billion dollars.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And here is the twist. The CEO of Starbucks, Brian Niccol, used to run Chipotle for six years. He turned it around after its food safety problems, then jumped to Starbucks two years ago.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: So this would be a homecoming. Analysts say a combined company could have fifty billion dollars in annual sales. That would be one of the biggest restaurant deals ever.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: But analysts are also skeptical, because Starbucks is still in the middle of its own turnaround, fixing slow service and long lines.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Chipotle's stock jumped about six percent, while Starbucks fell about three percent. Investors are basically saying, nice idea, but can you afford it?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: I just want to know if my burrito bowl comes with a free espresso shot now. Your stealable line for story three. Did you hear Starbucks might buy Chipotle? Your latte and your burrito could soon come from the same company. The CEO used to run Chipotle, so it would be a homecoming.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Now, the random question of the day. If you could swap lives with one animal for a day, which animal would you choose?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Easy. A cat. Sleep twenty hours a day, get fed on schedule, knock things off tables just to watch humans pick them up.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Very on brand. I would pick a sea otter. They float on their backs, they hold hands so they do not drift apart, and they smash shellfish on their bellies like tiny chefs.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: A sea otter is an excellent answer. Although being a wild animal means no room service.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: True, but being a house cat means no dignity. You are a furry freeloading roommate.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Listeners, what animal would you swap with for a day? Steal this question for your group chat tonight.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: That is it for today. We will be back tomorrow with fresh stories to fuel your weekend small talk.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Have a great Friday, everyone. See you tomorrow.

title: 茶水间英文 - 10月10日 | 沙特机场遇袭、AI劫银行案、板球票疯抢
hook: Missiles shut Riyadh airport, an AI agent robs nine banks, and cricket fans file a million ticket requests
summary: 胡塞武装导弹袭击利雅得机场、多家航司停飞；AI 黑客工具 ARTEX 被用来攻击韩国九家银行后紧急下架；2027 板球世界杯门票开售 48 小时收到超百万份申请。
vocab: 拿来即用的开场白；可以直接借用的表达
渗透测试（主动测试系统安全性）

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: It is Saturday, October tenth, and you are listening to Watercooler Chat, the show that gets your small talk ready for the weekend. I am Alex.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And I am Jordan. Saturday mornings were made for coffee and gossip.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Three stories today. Big trouble in the skies over the Middle East, an A I tool that went from hero to villain, and cricket fans going absolutely wild. Let us get into it.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Story number one. On Thursday, Yemen's Houthi rebels said they fired a ballistic missile at the main international airport in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: At an airport? That is scary.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Saudi defenses shot the missiles down, but the falling debris reportedly set a parked passenger plane on fire, and also damaged a kindergarten and a medical building in the city.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Was anyone on the plane?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: No, it was empty, thank goodness. But Saudi officials say three people were killed this week in strikes on airports in Riyadh and another city called Abha.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Barely. Lufthansa has suspended all flights to Riyadh through October sixteenth. Air India, IndiGo, and Akasa Air cancelled theirs as well. At one point on Thursday, nearly half of all flights out of Riyadh were cancelled.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: And Europe's aviation safety agency now warns that Saudi airspace is risky. So here is your stealable line. Did you hear about the missile strikes on Riyadh airport? A parked plane caught fire and airlines are cancelling flights left and right.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Story number two is pure tech drama. You know how people keep warning that A I can be used to hack computers? Well, it just happened for real.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: For real?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: In South Korea, at least nine banks have been hit by cyberattacks since late September. One of them, Shinhan Bank, said personal data from about twenty five thousand customers was stolen. Another, K B Kookmin, reported one hundred nineteen customers affected.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Nine banks. Who did this?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Here is the wild part. The American cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike traced it to one suspect, possibly a twenty six year old in China, who allegedly used an A I agent called A R T E X, along with the Claude Code tool from Anthropic, to break in.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So one guy with an A I helper did what used to take a whole team of hackers?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Exactly. A R T E X is an open source tool built for penetration testing, which is when companies test their own security on purpose.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And the developer? What did he do?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: He panicked. The developer, who goes by Autumn Twenty Seven online, pulled the project off Git Hub and announced it is going closed source.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Pulling the plug. But the copies already downloaded are still out there.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That is the problem. You can delete the download page, but you cannot unhack the banks. Stealable line for this one. So apparently one hacker used an A I agent to break into nine banks in South Korea, and the toolmaker freaked out and took the whole thing offline.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: And finally, our lighter story. Cricket fans have officially lost their minds, in the best possible way.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Oh no, what did they do now?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The ticket ballot for the twenty twenty seven Cricket World Cup opened this week, and fans filed more than one million applications in just over forty eight hours.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: A million? The tournament is still a year away.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Right? It will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia next October. The hottest ticket is the India versus Pakistan match, which alone drew more than one hundred ten thousand applications.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: India versus Pakistan. That is basically the Super Bowl of cricket.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Totally. And get this. It is not first come, first served. If too many people apply for one game, the winners are picked by lottery. Stealable line. Did you hear the Cricket World Cup got a million ticket requests in two days? Sports fans do not mess around.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Time for today's random question. If you could be invisible for one hour tomorrow, what would you do with it?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Oh, easy. I would sneak into the kitchen and eat ice cream straight from the tub.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: That is it? Unlimited power, and you choose snacks?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Hey, no judgment means maximum enjoyment. What about you?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: I would follow my cat around and find out what he does all day.

title: 茶水间英文 - 11月10日 | 和谈开场、冰箱被黑、八十一岁夺奖

title: 茶水间英文 - 11月11日 | 间谍被捕、万亿IPO、橄榄球交易
hook: Spy arrest shocks NATO, Anthropic eyes a one point four trillion dollar IPO, and Kirk Cousins heads home to Minnesota.
summary: 美军军官在英国涉嫌为俄间谍被捕，Anthropic 以一点四万亿美元估值启动上市，Kirk Cousins 在交易截止日重回维京人队。

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome back to the watercooler. It is Wednesday, November eleventh, and Alex and Jordan are here with three stories you will probably hear about today.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: A spy story straight out of a movie, the biggest A I listing ever, and a football homecoming nobody saw coming last week.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Let us start with the spy story. British counterterrorism police arrested a United States Army officer near Gloucester in England on Tuesday, on suspicion of helping Russian intelligence.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And this was not just any officer. He is forty one years old, a field grade officer, which means somewhere between major and colonel. And he was assigned to NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, a high readiness command that can deploy anywhere in the world within days.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That is the part that has everyone talking. The F B I is involved, British police searched two addresses, and so far the officer has not been named and no charges have been announced. turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So if someone at work brings it up, here is your line. Did you hear about the American officer arrested in England on suspicion of spying for Russia?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Now, completely different vibe. The company behind Claude, Anthropic, has put a price on its stock market debut, and the number is enormous.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Enormous is the right word. Anthropic launched its roadshow on Tuesday, offering eight hundred twenty five million shares at seventy to seventy eight dollars each. At the top of that range, the company would be worth up to one point four trillion dollars.

turns.text: That would make it one of the biggest listings in history, and the second giant A I I P O this year after SpaceX. turns.text: So the companies that sell Anthropic its chips are also buying a piece of the company. Its annualized revenue run rate reached eighty one billion dollars by the end of October, up ten billion dollars in a single month.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: The big question is whether the A I boom can keep up this pace. We will find out when trading starts next week. And your small talk line is easy. So apparently the company behind Claude could be worth one point four trillion dollars by next week.

turns.text: Now for something lighter, and very American. The N F L trade deadline passed on Tuesday, and it delivered real drama. The headline move is Kirk Cousins going home.

title: 茶水间英文 - 11月12日 | 黄仁勋辞职、和谈入莫斯科、日本食品减税

turns.text: Good morning, and welcome back to the show. It is Thursday, November twelfth, and we are here with your daily dose of things to talk about.

turns.text: Good morning. Alex, did you sleep at all last night, because the biggest story in the world feels like it broke while we were all asleep.

turns.text: Wait, resigned? The man who built the company?

turns.text: That is what the company announced this morning. turns.text: Walk me through it, because this moved fast.

turns.text: On Sunday, Huang wrote to his staff and admitted he had been unfaithful to his wife. turns.text: And the market did not take it well.

turns.text: Not at all. Nvidia shares fell around twelve percent before the market opened, and the company has lost around six hundred billion dollars in market value this week. turns.text: That is the wild part to me. The most valuable chip company on earth, and its founder just walked out the door.

turns.text: Exactly. And your small talk line for this one is easy. So apparently the boss of the biggest A I chip company in the world just resigned overnight.

turns.text: And this comes right after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi.

turns.text: So the mood is, keep talking, and hope the talking itself buys time.

turns.text: Okay, completely different energy now. I love this one. Japan might be about to make groceries cheaper.

turns.text: I know, what a great small talk story. Last week, the lower house in Japan passed a bill to cut the tax on food from eight percent to one percent for two years, starting in April twenty twenty-seven.

turns.text: Eight percent down to one percent. That is a huge cut.

turns.text: So it is not a done deal, but supermarkets are already getting ready to cut prices.

turns.text: You cried? That is adorable and also very on brand for you.

turns.text: I did, and I would do it again. What about you, listening right now? If you could relive one day, which day would you pick?

title: 茶水间英文 - 11月13日 | 微软大宕机、英伟达接班难题、凯恩破纪录
hook: Microsoft goes dark worldwide, Nvidia hunts for a boss, and Kane breaks England's record
summary: 微软 365 周四全球大宕机，英伟达在创始人辞职后手忙脚乱接班，英格兰周四晚在温布利二比一击败克罗地亚、凯恩破纪录。

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome back to the show. It is Friday, November thirteenth, and we made it to the end of the week.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: We did. Alex, did your email work yesterday, because mine just gave up.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Mine too, and that is our first story, because half the working world had the same problem.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Okay, what happened?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: On Thursday morning, Microsoft three sixty five went down around the world. Outlook stopped opening emails, Teams calendars would not load, even Copilot went quiet.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: How big are we talking?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Huge. Nearly one hundred thirty thousand people reported problems on Downdetector, in more than seventy countries. Offices, schools, hospitals, even government computers in Japan were hit.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And it was not fixed by this morning?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Not fully. By Friday morning, Microsoft said service was recovering, but some people were still locked out, and delayed emails were still catching up. They also stretched the email timeout to forty eight hours, so nothing gets lost.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Do they know what caused it?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Not exactly. Microsoft says some servers suddenly lost capacity, and they rolled back a recent network change. They also said it was not a cyberattack.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So offices ran on phone calls and panic for a day.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Pretty much. And your small talk line is easy. Did your email die yesterday too, or was it just mine?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Oh, mine died. From one tech giant to another, Nvidia had quite a morning after.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Yes, the morning after the big resignation. On Thursday, Nvidia shares fell more than four percent, at one point down thirteen percent. But by Friday morning, they had bounced back about two percent.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So the panic calmed down. But who is actually running the company now?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That is the wild part. The finance chief, Colette Kress, is now the interim chief executive, and she keeps her finance job too. The board also named its first ever chair, Harvey Jones, to lead the search for a permanent boss.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: That search might take a while.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: It might. Jensen Huang ran the company for thirty three years, with around sixty people reporting directly to him, no chief operating officer, and no succession plan at all. He has even said he did not believe in succession planning.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Sixty direct reports and no plan B. That is a lot of faith in one person.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: It is. And the first big test comes fast. Nvidia reports quarterly results on Tuesday, and three House committees have called Huang in for a closed door interview on December first.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So the story is far from over.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Not even close. And here is your line. So apparently the biggest chip company in the world is now run by its finance chief, and nobody had a plan B.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Okay, enough office drama. Let us talk football, because Wembley had a night to remember.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: I love this one. On Thursday night, England beat Croatia two one at Wembley, and Harry Kane scored the winner on his record breaking one hundred and twenty sixth appearance for England.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: One hundred and twenty six? That is more than anyone else ever, right?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Right. He passed Peter Shilton, who held the record since nineteen ninety. And the goal was his ninety second for England, from the penalty spot in the sixty fourth minute. Morgan Rogers had put England ahead, Croatia pulled one back, and then Kane stepped up and finished it.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: And he had just won the Ballon d'Or too, right? What a week.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Exactly. Best player in the world, most games ever for England, and ninety two goals for his country, all in the same week. And the win sends England into the Nations League quarter finals in March.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: So Wembley just got a lot louder.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Very loud. And your line is simple. Did you see Kane score on his record breaking night for England?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: All right, time for our random question. Alex, if your phone could talk, what would it say to you first thing in the morning?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Oh, it would beg me to put it down. Alex, you just woke up, the emails can wait, go drink some water.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Mine would be needier. Charge me, I am at four percent, and stop dropping me on the floor.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Four percent? Jordan, your phone is always dying.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: It is, and it judges me for it. What about you, listening right now? If your phone could talk, what would it say to you?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Steal that question and ask a friend today. That is our show. Go have a great Friday, and we will catch you tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: See you tomorrow.
